senses.definition_en: Senses relating to literal movement.; to arrive

examples.english: The train arrives at 2 o'clock.
examples.text: El tren viene a las 2.
examples.translation: The train arrives at 2 o'clock.

senses.definition_en: Figurative senses.; to come from, originate

examples.english: I am from Morelos. / I come from Morelos.
examples.text: Vengo de Morelos.
examples.translation: I am from Morelos. / I come from Morelos.

examples.english: The word fútbol in Spanish comes from the English word football.
examples.text: La palabra fútbol en español viene de la palabra inglesa football.
examples.translation: The word fútbol in Spanish comes from the English word football.

examples.english: My friend comes from a poor family.
examples.text: Mi amiga viene de una familia pobre.
examples.translation: My friend comes from a poor family.

examples.english: Chinese rice is a kind of food, [just because it has "Chinese" in the name] it doesn't mean it comes from China. If you order Chinese rice in Colombia [and] the US you are going to get the same fried rice. You are acting like all the chicken from KFC comes from the US.
examples.text: Arroz chino es un tipo [de comida,] no significa que viene de [China]. Si usted pide arroz chino en Colombia o Chinese rice en los Estados Unidos usted va a recibir el mismo arroz frito. Usted actúa como si todo el pollo de KFC viniera de los Estados Unidos.
examples.translation: Chinese rice is a kind of food, [just because it has "Chinese" in the name] it doesn't mean it comes from China. If you order Chinese rice in Colombia [and] the US you are going to get the same fried rice. You are acting like all the chicken from KFC comes from the US.

examples.english: Almost 30% of Australia’s GDP comes from its industry, and 60% from its services. In Norway, nearly 37% comes from industry, mainly energy, construction, and mining.
examples.text: Casi el 30% del PBI de [A]ustralia viene de su industria, y el 60% de sus servicios. En [N]oruega casi el 37% viene de la industria, principalmente de energía, construcción y minería.
examples.translation: Almost 30% of Australia’s GDP comes from its industry, and 60% from its services. In Norway, nearly 37% comes from industry, mainly energy, construction, and mining.

senses.definition_en: Figurative senses.; to come (happen)

examples.english: Whatever comes (happens), I'll accept.
examples.text: Lo que venga, lo acepto.
examples.translation: Whatever comes (happens), I'll accept.

senses.definition_en: Figurative senses.; to come (appear)

examples.english: Friendships come and go.

senses.definition_en: Figurative senses.; to come (to have some characteristic or quality) (with an adjective or prepositional phrase)

examples.english: These water bottles come in packs of 4 and 6.
examples.text: Estas botellas de agua vienen en packs de 4 y 6.
examples.translation: These water bottles come in packs of 4 and 6.

examples.english: Letters come in envelopes so they don't get damaged.
examples.text: Las cartas vienen en sobres para que no se estropeen.
examples.translation: Letters come in envelopes so they don't get damaged.

glosses: to come (to have some characteristic or quality) (with an adjective or prepositional phrase)

senses.definition_en: Figurative senses.; to receive something, get something

examples.english: I got your package. / Your package arrived.
examples.text: Me vino tu paquete.
examples.translation: I got your package. / Your package arrived.

examples.english: I got an email from you.
examples.text: Me vino un email tuyo.
examples.translation: I got an email from you.

examples.english: When I was a kid I got a toy I loved in a Nesquik cereal box and one day I lost it.
examples.text: De niño me vino un juguete que me encantaba con los cereales de Nesquik y un día lo perdí.
examples.translation: When I was a kid I got a toy I loved in a Nesquik cereal box and one day I lost it.

senses.definition_en: Figurative senses.; to get (something felt in one's body or perceived in one's mind, a feeling, an illness, pain, an urge, an idea, etc.)

examples.text: Near-synonyms: dar, tener

examples.english: Last week I got a migraine so bad I thought I was going to die.
examples.text: La semana pasada me vino una migraña tan fuerte que pensé que me iba a morir.
examples.translation: Last week I got a migraine so bad I thought I was going to die.

glosses: to get (something felt in one's body or perceived in one's mind, a feeling, an illness, pain, an urge, an idea, etc.)

senses.definition_en: Figurative senses.; to be coming or coming up (of a date, event, etc.)

examples.english: Christmas is coming, so start putting up the tree.
examples.text: Ya viene Navidad, así que vete haciendo el árbol.
examples.translation: Christmas is coming, so start putting up the tree.

glosses: to be coming or coming up (of a date, event, etc.)

examples.translation: next week (literally "the week that comes")

examples.english: next Thursday (literally "the Thursday that comes")
examples.text: el jueves que viene
examples.translation: next Thursday (literally "the Thursday that comes")

examples.translation: What's that about? / Why did (you/they) do that? / Why did that happen? / etc.

senses.definition_en: Figurative senses.; translated with end up

senses.definition_en: Figurative senses.; to be (with "bien" (convenient, helpful, good), "mal" (bad), etc.)

examples.english: Thanks for the feedback, it's helpful (for me).
examples.text: Gracias por la crítica, me viene bien.
examples.translation: Thanks for the feedback, it's helpful (for me).

examples.english: Does Thursday work for you to grab a drink?
examples.text: ¿Te viene bien el jueves para tomar algo?
examples.translation: Does Thursday work for you to grab a drink?

examples.english: Digital books are very practical, I can take them with me everywhere and read whichever one I want, and switch whenever I want. At my age, it's helpful to be able to change the font size and/or the background color. I can zoom in on images to see details. I have a built-in dictionary in several languages. I can search Google for images of things I want to see what they look like or look up references.
examples.text: Los libros digitales son muy prácticos, puedo llevarlos conmigo a todos lados y leer el que quiera y cambiar cuando quiero. A mí edad me viene bien poder cambiar el tamaño de la letra y o el color del fondo. Puedo agrandar las imágenes para ver detalle. Tengo diccionario incluido en varios idiomas. Puedo buscar en Google imágenes de cosas que quiero ver cómo son o buscar referencias.
examples.translation: Digital books are very practical, I can take them with me everywhere and read whichever one I want, and switch whenever I want. At my age, it's helpful to be able to change the font size and/or the background color. I can zoom in on images to see details. I have a built-in dictionary in several languages. I can search Google for images of things I want to see what they look like or look up references.
